TITLE: Investigating Low-Rank Adaptation for MPC-Based Privacy-Preserving Fine-Tuning of LLMs
PROPOSAL: We will adapt the low-rank adaptation method, LoRA, to the MPC setting to reduce the number of parameters that need to be updated during fine-tuning, thus decreasing communication overhead. We will compare the performance of MPC-based LoRA with vanilla MPC-based fine-tuning on several benchmark datasets, including sentiment classification and news topic classification.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Communication-Reduced MPC Framework for LLM Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We propose to design and implement a communication-reduced MPC framework for fine-tuning LLMs, focusing on approximating the computationally expensive operations (Softmax, GELU, LayerNorm) in forward and backward propagation using efficient MPC protocols such as oblivious transfers and homomorphic encryption, and develop a novel compression technique to shrink the size of messages exchanged during MPC protocols. We plan to test our approach on synthetic data to evaluate its performance and efficiency.
CONTROLS: Compare with the standard MPC protocol and a baseline that only supports linear operations.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to achieve a speedup of 2-3 times over the standard MPC protocol while maintaining similar accuracy, which could fail if the approximation of complex operations compromises the model performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust MPC Protocols for Nonlinear Operations in Backward Propagation
PROPOSAL: We aim to develop and implement novel MPC protocols that securely perform the nonlinear operations in backward propagation (e.g., derivatives of Softmax and GELU) using robust and private protocols such as the Fairplay protocol and the Tree-based Oblivious Transfer protocol. These protocols will be integrated into our communication-reduced MPC framework (Proposal 1) to improve efficiency and robustness.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed protocols with existing MPC protocols and evaluate their robustness against Byzantine failures.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our robust MPC protocols will significantly reduce the communication overhead and improve the accuracy of the fine-tuned LLMs, which may fail if the protocols are not efficiently scalable to large-scale LLMs.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Efficient Communication-Reduced MPC Framework for LLM Fine-Tuning with Gradient Compression
PROPOSAL: We propose to extend the communication-reduced MPC framework (Proposal 1) by incorporating gradient compression techniques, such as quantization and gradient sparsification, to reduce the size of the gradients exchanged during MPC protocols. This will alleviate the communication bottleneck in backward propagation and improve the overall efficiency of the framework.
CONTROLS: Compare with the standard MPC protocol and the original communication-reduced MPC framework (Proposal 1) without gradient compression.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to achieve a further speedup of 1.5-2 times over the original framework, which could fail if the gradient compression techniques compromise the model accuracy.

By adapting only a low-rank component of the model, we aim to minimize the communication overhead and preserve the model's performance.
CONTROLS: Compare with full-parameter fine-tuning and the original communication-reduced MPC framework (Proposal 1) without low-rank adaptation.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate that low-rank adaptation will significantly reduce the communication and computation costs without compromising the model's performance, which may fail if the low-rank approximation is not accurate enough.

This will improve the robustness and reliability of the protocols and prevent potential faults in the fine-tuning process.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original robust MPC protocols (Proposal 2) without error correction and evaluate the impact on the fine-tuning accuracy.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to achieve improved robustness and reliability of the MPC protocols, which may fail if the error correction mechanism introduces additional latency or overhead that compromises the fine-tuning performance.

This will provide a robust and trustworthy framework for fine-tuning LLMs in sensitive domains such as healthcare and finance.
